metadata.title: Breathe: Paige's Journey
metadata.adaptation_concept: Feminist reinterpretation focusing on Paige Wynorski

primary.name: Paige Wynorski
primary.occupation: Medical researcher and part-time historical interpreter
primary.backstory: Brilliant researcher whose career has been sidelined by caring for her mother with dementia. Uses her knowledge of psychology to navigate complex power dynamics.

secondary.name: Victor Mancini
secondary.relationship_to_protagonist: Patient at mother's care facility, con artist with sexual addiction

secondary.name: Ida Mancini
secondary.relationship_to_protagonist: Patient with dementia, former radical feminist activist

secondary.name: Dr. Marshall
secondary.relationship_to_protagonist: Hospital administrator who undervalues Paige's research

chapters.title: Algorithms and Colonial Village
chapters.setting: Colonial theme park and research laboratory
chapters.summary: Paige introduces her dual life as a medical researcher and historical interpreter at a colonial village. She reveals her research on neural pathways and dementia treatments, which the hospital administration consistently undermines. Her inner monologue reveals her growing frustration with institutional sexism in the research field while she codes a neural network in Julia to analyze her mother's brain scans.
key_events: Paige's research presentation is interrupted and dismissed by male colleagues
Paige meets Victor at the colonial village where she works part-time
Paige begins writing a revolutionary algorithm in Julia that could predict dementia progression
chapters.dialogue_excerpt: "The thing about neural networks," I say to no one as my fingers fly across the keyboard, "is that they're perfect metaphors for human connections. We're all just running our own algorithms based on our training data. My mother's brain is rewriting its own code now, and I'm going to crack it before it's too late."

chapters.title: Pattern Recognition
chapters.summary: Paige's visits to her mother reveal complex layers of their relationship. She begins to see patterns in her mother's seemingly random behavior that mirror patterns in her data. Meanwhile, she observes Victor's choking scam but recognizes it as a psychological coping mechanism rather than simply a con.
key_events: Paige discovers her mother's hidden journal documenting radical feminist activism
Paige witnesses Victor's choking routine and analyzes it from a psychological perspective
Paige's Julia program begins showing promising results in predicting neural degradation patterns
chapters.dialogue_excerpt: "There's a structure to chaos," I tell my mother, who stares blankly at the wall. "Your mind isn't gone—it's just reorganizing itself according to different rules. I'm learning to speak your new language."

chapters.title: Historic Reconstructions
chapters.summary: Paige draws parallels between historical reenactment and how we construct our identities. She begins implementing her mother's radical feminist philosophy into her research approach, challenging institutional norms while developing her groundbreaking algorithm.
key_events: Paige confronts Dr. Marshall about gender bias in research funding
Paige uses colonial village performance to process psychological insights
Paige discovers a breakthrough in her mother's journal that connects to her research
chapters.dialogue_excerpt: "You want authenticity?" I ask the tourists watching me churn butter in my colonial costume. "Authentic history would show you that women have always been rebelling against constraints, always writing code that wasn't meant for us to write. My mother understood that. Now I do too."

themes.name: Autonomy versus Dependency
themes.exploration: Paige struggles between caring for her mother and pursuing her groundbreaking research, representing the broader conflict women face between nurturing roles and self-actualization.

themes.name: Institutional Sexism in Science
themes.exploration: Paige's brilliant research is consistently undervalued and underfunded compared to male colleagues with less innovative ideas.

themes.name: Technology as Liberation
themes.exploration: Paige's growing expertise in Julia programming becomes a metaphor for creating new languages and systems outside patriarchal structures.

themes.name: Bodily Autonomy
themes.exploration: Through Paige's research on the brain and her observations of her mother's dementia, the novel explores questions of selfhood, consciousness, and who controls women's bodies and minds.

julia_code_excerpts.context: Paige developing a neural network model
julia_code_excerpts.code:
using Flux
using Statistics
using DataFrames

# Neural pathway degradation model
function build_dementia_model(input_size, hidden_size, output_size)
    return Chain(
        Dense(input_size, hidden_size, relu),
        Dropout(0.2),
        Dense(hidden_size, hidden_size, relu),
        Dense(hidden_size, output_size),
        softmax
    )
end

# Paige's innovation: incorporating feminist theory into neural networks
function feminist_loss_function(y_pred, y_true)
    # Standard loss function but with weighted penalties for false negatives
    # Represents Paige's understanding that medical research historically
    # undervalues women's symptoms
    standard_loss = Flux.crossentropy(y_pred, y_true)
    gender_bias_correction = calculate_bias_factor(y_pred, y_true)
    return standard_loss * gender_bias_correction
end

julia_code_excerpts.context: Paige analyzing her mother's speech patterns
julia_code_excerpts.code:
using TextAnalysis
using Plots

# Text analysis of mother's journals across time
function analyze_linguistic_degradation(journal_entries)
    corpus = Corpus([StringDocument(entry.text) for entry in journal_entries])
    prepare!(corpus, strip_articles, strip_pronouns)
    m = DocumentTermMatrix(corpus)
    
    # Track changes in linguistic complexity over time
    complexity_scores = []
    for i in 1:length(journal_entries)
        doc = corpus[i]
        score = lexical_diversity(doc) * syntactic_complexity(doc)
        push!(complexity_scores, score)
    end
    
    # Plot the degradation pattern
    plot(journal_entries.date, complexity_scores, 
         title="Linguistic Complexity Over Time",
         xlabel="Date", ylabel="Complexity Score",
         legend=false)
end

key_passages.title: On Identity and Performance
key_passages.text: Every day I put on someone else's clothes. Colonial dress at the village, lab coat at the hospital, daughter at my mother's bedside. Men get to wear one identity their whole lives. My mother wore so many she eventually forgot which one was real. Now I'm picking through her collection, trying them on one by one, seeing which ones have power and which ones are just costumes. The Julia code I write at night is the only place where I'm fully myself—building worlds with rules I create.

key_passages.title: On Medical Patriarchy
key_passages.text: Dr. Marshall reviews my research with his legs spread wide, consuming all available space. 'Interesting approach, Paige, but perhaps a bit too experimental.' Translation: too female, too innovative, too threatening. I smile and nod while mentally adding another variable to my algorithm. One that accounts for the systematic dismissal of women's intellectual contributions. The model improves by 23% when I factor in society's resistance to paradigm shifts proposed by women.

key_passages.title: Confrontation at the Hospital Board
key_passages.text: "Your funding proposal has been denied," Dr. Marshall says without looking up. I stand my ground, my mother's journal in my bag giving me strength. "I'd like to know specifically which methodological concerns the board had." He blinks, surprised I haven't left. "We just don't see the priority in dementia research focused on female patients." And there it is. The same bias that has killed women in emergency rooms, that has left female pain unresearched, that assumes male is the default human. I place my latest results on his desk. "Women make up 66% of Alzheimer's patients. My algorithm predicts progression patterns with 82% accuracy. Your choice is to fund groundbreaking research by a woman or watch someone else do it."

narrative_structure_notes: This rewrite transforms the story from Victor's sex addiction and con artistry to Paige's intellectual journey and fight for recognition. Her work with Julia programming creates a metaphor for building new systems of thought outside patriarchal frameworks. The story maintains dark humor but centers female autonomy in scientific, personal, and sexual realms.
